transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because... even on my better days, I just can't shake this feeling. I keep thinking that some of the people at my church, and in my walking club, are watching me. And it feels like they're putting little messages about me in the church bulletin, or hiding them in the things they say when I'm around. It's just very unsettling.
How long have you been experiencing these feelings about people watching you and leaving messages?
It's been about eleven months now. The messages, and... well, the voices too, and just having trouble keeping my thoughts straight... all of it has been happening for about eleven months.
During these past eleven months, have you also experienced any significant periods where your mood was extremely low or, alternatively, unusually high and energetic?

Well, yes. I haven't really had any times where I felt unusually high or energetic, but I have had some very low periods. There was a time when I was at my absolute lowest... I was barely eating, and I just kept thinking that I had failed everyone in my life. And even during that really dark time, I was still hearing my friend's voice when she wasn't there, and I still believed the people at church were sending those hidden messages about me. It all just happened at the same time.
During those eleven months of hearing voices and feeling watched, how much of that time would you say you were also feeling that very low, depressed mood?

Well, I'd say for most of this whole stretch. The sadness, the guilt about failing people, just... not caring about my walking club or anything else... it's been there in the background almost the whole time. Even on the days when the voices were quieter, or I wasn't as worried about the church bulletin, that low feeling was still just sitting there with me.
